questions.q:
If $K_\rho$ for a reaction,
$A(g)+2 B(g) \rightleftharpoons 3 C(g)+D(g)$ is 0.05 atm at 1000 K . Its $K_{\mathrm{c}}$ in term of $R$ is $\frac{x \times 10^{-5}}{R}$. The value of $x$ is ______
questions.solution:
Given reaction,
$\begin{aligned}
& A(g)+2 B(g) \rightleftharpoons 3 C(g)+D(g) \\
& \Delta n_g=4-3=1
\end{aligned}$
Formula for $K_p$,
$\begin{aligned}
K_p & =K_c(R T)^{\Delta n} \\
0.05 & =K_c(R \times 1000)^1 \\
K_c & =\frac{5 \times 10^{-5}}{R}
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: For a first order reaction, time required for $99 \%$ completion of a reaction is $x$ times the time required for completion of $90 \%$. The value of $x$ is .......
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
t_{99 \%} & =\frac{2.303}{k} \log \frac{(a)}{a-0.99 a} \\
& =\frac{2.303}{k} \log 10^2 \Rightarrow 2 \times \frac{2.303}{k} ...(i)\\
t_{90 \%} & =\frac{2.303}{k} \log \frac{a}{a-0.90 a} \\
& =\frac{2.303}{k} \log 10=\frac{2.303}{k}...(ii)
\end{aligned}$
Take the ratio of (i) and (ii)
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{t_{99 \%}}{t_{90 \%}}=2 \\
& t_{99 \%}=2 \times t_{90 \%}
\end{aligned}$
Hence, 2 times is the final answer.

questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: Electronegativity of the following elements increases in the order
questions.solution:
As electronegativity increases across the period, therefore, electronegativity of nitrogen ( N ) is more than carbon (C) and electronegativity of $P$ is more than Si .
Also electronegativity decreases down the group, therefore electronegativity of carbon is more than Si and electronegativity of $N$ is more than $P$. Hence, the correct increasing order will be Si, P, C, N.

questions.q: $F_2$ is formed by reacting $\mathrm{K}_2 \mathrm{MnF}_6$ with
questions.solution:

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Given $\frac{d y}{d x}+2 y \tan x=\sin x$ and $y=0$ for $x=\frac{\pi}{3}$. If maximum value of $y$ is $\frac{1}{k}$, then ' $k$ ' is equal to
questions.solution:
$\frac{d y}{d x}+2 y \tan x=\sin x$
The given differential equation is of the form
$\frac{d y}{d x}+P y=Q$
By comparing, we get
$P=2 \tan x$ and $Q=\sin x\therefore$ I.F. $=e^{\int \cdot 2 \tan \cdot d x}=e^{2 \log \sec x}=e^{\log \sec ^2 x}=\sec ^2 x$
Then, solution of the differential equation
$\begin{aligned}
& y \sec ^2 x=\int \sin x \cdot \sec ^2 x \cdot d x+c \\
\Rightarrow & y \sec ^2 x=\int \frac{\sin x}{\cos ^2 x} d x+c \\
\Rightarrow & y \sec ^2 x=\int \tan x \cdot \sec x d x+c \\
\Rightarrow & y \sec ^2 x=\sec x+c \\
\Rightarrow & y=\frac{1}{\sec x}+\frac{c}{\sec ^2 x}=\cos x+\left(\cos ^2 x\right) \cdot c \\
\text { at } & x=\frac{\pi}{3}, y=0 \\
\therefore & 0=\cos \frac{\pi}{3}+\left(\cos ^2 \frac{\pi}{3} \cdot c\right) \\
\Rightarrow & 0=\frac{1}{2}+\frac{c}{4} \Rightarrow c=-2 \\
\therefore & y=\cos x-2 \cos ^2 x
\end{aligned}\Rightarrow \frac{y}{2}=-\cos ^2 x+\frac{1}{2} \cos x=-\left(\cos ^2 x-\frac{1}{2} \cos x\right)\Rightarrow \frac{y}{2}=-\left[\left(\cos x-\frac{1}{4}\right)^2-\left(\frac{1}{4}\right)^2\right]=-\left[\left(\cos x-\frac{1}{4}\right)^2\right]+\frac{1}{16}$
So, maximum value of $\frac{y}{2}=\frac{1}{16}\Rightarrow$ Maximum value of $y=\frac{1}{8} \Rightarrow k=8$

differentiating the equation,
$\Rightarrow f^{\prime}(y)+2 x=f^{\prime}(x+y)$
at $y=0f^{\prime}(0)+2 x=f^{\prime}(x)\Rightarrow f^{\prime}(x)=2 x$
Integrating both sides.
$\int f^{\prime}(x)=\int 2 x \cdot d x\Rightarrow f(x)=x^2\therefore I=\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}} f(\sin x) d x\Rightarrow I=\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}} \sin ^2 x \cdot d x...(ii)\Rightarrow I=\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}} \sin ^2\left(\frac{\pi}{2}-x\right) d x=\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}} \cos ^2 x \cdot d x \ldots(iii)$
Adding Eqs. (ii) and (iii)
$2l=\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\left(\sin ^2 x+\cos ^2 x\right) d x=\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}} 1 \cdot d x\begin{array}{ll}\Rightarrow & 2l=\frac{\pi}{2} \\ \Rightarrow & l=\frac{\pi}{4}\end{array}$

questions.q: If $x=\sin \left(2 \tan ^{-1} 2\right), y=\sin \left(\frac{1}{2} \tan ^{-1} \frac{4}{3}\right)$, then
questions.solution:
we have \(x=\sin \left(2 \tan ^{-1} 2\right)\),
\(\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow x=\sin (2 \theta), \tan ^{-1} 2=\theta \\
& \Rightarrow x=\frac{2 \tan \theta}{1+\tan ^2 \theta}, \tan \theta=2 \\
& \Rightarrow x=\frac{4}{5}

Also, \(y=\sin \left(\frac{1}{2} \tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{4}{3}\right)\right)\)
\(\begin{array}{ll}

\Rightarrow & y=\sin (\theta), \tan (\theta)=\frac{1}{2} \\
\Rightarrow & y=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}
\end{array}\)
Hence, \(y^2=\frac{1}{5}=1-\frac{4}{5}=1-x\)

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Let $f(x)=\left[\frac{\sin x}{x}\right]+\left[\frac{2 \sin x}{x}\right]+\ldots+\left[\frac{10 \sin x}{x}\right]$ (where [.] is the largest integer). then, find the value of $\lim _{x \rightarrow 0} f(x)$.
questions.solution:
As we know,
$\lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{\sin x}{x} \simeq 1$
but it is actually less than 1 .
So, $\lim _{x \rightarrow 0}\left[\frac{\sin x}{x}\right]=0=1^2-1$
Similarly, $\lim _{x \rightarrow 0}\left[2 \frac{\sin 2 x}{x}\right]=\lim _{x \rightarrow 0}\left[4 \frac{\sin 2 x}{2 x}\right]=3=2^2-1$
Hence, $\lim _{x \rightarrow 0}\left[n \frac{\sin n x}{x}\right]=n^2-1$
Therefore,
$\begin{aligned}
& \lim _{x \rightarrow 0} f(x)=\left(1^2-1\right)+\left(2^2-1\right)+\ldots+\left(10^2-(1)\right. \\
& =\left(1^2+2^2+\ldots+10^2\right)-(1+1+\ldots+1 \text { times }) \\
& =\frac{10 \times 11 \times 21}{6}-10 \\
& =385-10=375
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Let $D=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}n & n^2 & n^3 \\ n^2 & n^3 & n^5 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{array}\right|$, then $\lim _{n \rightarrow \infty} \frac{M_{11}+C_{33}}{\left(M_{13}\right)^2}$ is equal to (where $M_{i j}$ is the minor and $C_{i j}$ is the cofactor of $i^{\text {th }}$ row and $j^{\text {th }}$ column's element)
questions.solution:
$\because D=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}
n & n^2 & n^3 \\
n^2 & n^3 & n^5 \\
1 & 2 & 3
\end{array}\right|$
Then, $M_{11}=\left|\begin{array}{cc}n^3 & n^5 \\ 2 & 3\end{array}\right|=3 n^3-2 n^5$
and $C_{33}=\left|\begin{array}{cc}n & n^2 \\ n^2 & n^3\end{array}\right|=n^4-n^4=0\begin{aligned}
M_{13} & =\left|\begin{array}{cc}
n^2 & n^3 \\
1 & 2
\end{array}\right|=2 n^2-n^3 \\
\therefore  \lim _{n \rightarrow \infty} & =\frac{M_{11}+C_{33}}{\left(M_{13}\right)^2}=\lim _{n \rightarrow \infty} \frac{n^3\left(3-2 n^2\right)+0}{n^4(2-n)^2} \\
& =\lim _{n \rightarrow \infty} \frac{3-2 n^2}{n\left[4+n^2-4 n\right]}=\lim _{n \rightarrow \infty} \frac{n^2\left(\frac{3}{n^2}-2\right)}{n^3\left(\frac{4}{n^2}+1-\frac{4}{n}\right)}
\end{aligned}$
put $n=\infty=\frac{\left(\frac{3}{\infty^2}-2\right)}{\infty\left(\frac{4}{\infty^2}+1-\frac{4}{\infty}\right)}=\frac{-2}{1 \times \infty}=0$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If two tangents drawn from the point $(h, k)$ to the parabola $y^2=64 x$ be such that the slope of one tangent is 8 times of the other, then the value of $\frac{k^2}{2 h}$ is
questions.solution:
Let the equation of tangent is
$y=m x+\frac{16}{m} [\because a=16]$
It passes through $(h, k)$
Then, $k=m h+\frac{16}{m} \Rightarrow m^2 h+16-m k=0$
According to the question, roots of the equation will be $m_1$ and $8 m_1$.
So, $m_1+8 m_1=\frac{k}{h} \Rightarrow 9 m_1=\frac{k}{h}...(i)$
and $m_1 \cdot 8 m_1=\frac{16}{h} \Rightarrow 8 m_1^2=\frac{16}{h}...(ii)$
By solving these equations, we get
$\frac{k^2}{2 h}=81$

questions.q: If $N$ denotes number of 8 digit numbers that contains exactly four nines, then unit digit of $N$ is

$\begin{aligned}
\Rightarrow N & =\text { Number with }\left[\left\{1^{\text {st }} \text { digit is } 9\right\}+\left\{1^{\text {st }} \text { digit is not } 9\right\}\right] \\

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: In triangle $A B C, \sin A, \sin B$ and $\sin C$ are in $A P\left(C\gt90^{\circ}\right)$, then $\cos A$ is
questions.solution:
As we know,
$\frac{\sin A}{a}=\frac{\sin B}{b}=\frac{\sin C}{c}$
and $\sin A, \sin B$ and $\sin C$ are in $A P$.
So, $a, b, c$ will also be in AP
$\begin{aligned}
\therefore 2 b & =a+c \\
\text { and } \cos A & =\frac{b^2+c^2-a^2}{2 b c}=\frac{b^2+c^2-(2 b-c)^2}{2 b c} \\
& =\frac{b^2+c^2-\left(4 b^2+c^2-4 b c\right)}{2 b c} \\
& =\frac{-3 b^2+4 b c}{2 b c} \\
& =\frac{b(4 c-3 b)}{2 b c}=\frac{4 c-3 b}{2 c}
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If in a $\triangle A B C, \sin ^2 A+\sin ^2 B+\sin ^2 C=2$, then the triangle is always:
questions.solution:
$\sin ^2 A+\sin ^2 B+\sin ^2 C=2= \frac{1-\cos 2 A}{2}+\frac{1-\cos 2 B}{2}+\frac{1-\cos 2 C}{2}=2\Rightarrow \cos 2 A+\cos 2 B+\cos 2 C=-1\Rightarrow 2 \cos (A+B) \cos (A-B)=-2 \cos ^2 C\Rightarrow 2 \cos (\pi-C) \cos (A-B)=-2 \cos ^2 C{[\because A+B+C=\pi] }\Rightarrow 2 \cos C[\cos C-\cos (A-B)]=0\Rightarrow -2 \cos C[\cos (A+B)+\cos (A-B)]=0\Rightarrow -\cos A \cdot \cos B \cdot \cos C=0\Rightarrow \cos A \cdot \cos B \cdot \cos C=0$
Therefore, one of them should be equal to zero.
So, exactly one angle is $90^{\circ}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If expression $x+\frac{1}{x^2},|x\gt0|$ attains is minimum value at $x=\alpha$, then $\alpha^3$ is
questions.solution:
$\because  x+\frac{1}{x^2}=\frac{x}{2}+\frac{x}{2}+\frac{1}{x^2}\text {and } \mathrm{AM} \geq \mathrm{GM}\Rightarrow  \frac{x}{2}+\frac{x}{2}+\frac{1}{x^2} \geq\left(\frac{x}{2} \times \frac{x}{2} \times \frac{1}{x^2}\right)^{\frac{1}{3}}\Rightarrow  \frac{x}{2}+\frac{x}{2}+\frac{1}{x^2} \geq\left(\frac{1}{4}\right)^{\frac{1}{3}}$
Minimum value of $x+\frac{1}{x^2}=\sqrt[3]{\frac{1}{4}}$
and for minimum value
$\frac{x}{2}=\frac{1}{x^2} \Rightarrow x^3=2$
Hence, $\alpha^3=2$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If the angle between the pair of straight lines formed by joining the points of intersection of $x^2+y^2=4$ and $y=3 x+c$ to the origin is a right angle, then $c^2$ is
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
&  \because x^2+y^2=4 \Rightarrow x^2+y^2-4(1)^2=0 ...(i)\\
& \text { and } y=3 x+c \Rightarrow \frac{y-3 x}{c}=1
\end{aligned}$
Put the value of ' 1 ' in Eq. (i)
$\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow  x^2+y^2-4\left(\frac{y-3 x}{c}\right)^2=0 \\
& \Rightarrow  x^2+y^2-4\left(\left(\frac{y}{c}\right)^2+\left(\frac{3 x}{c}\right)^2-\frac{6 x y}{c^2}\right)=0 \\
& \Rightarrow  x^2\left(1-\frac{36}{c^2}\right)+y^2\left(1-\frac{4}{c^2}\right)+\frac{24 x y}{c^2}=0
\end{aligned}$
According to the question,
$\begin{aligned}
& \left(1-\frac{36}{c^2}\right)+\left(1-\frac{4}{c^2}\right)=0 \Rightarrow 2=\frac{40}{c^2} \\
\Rightarrow & \quad c^2=20
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: When 100 V DC is applied across a solenoid, a current of 1 A flows in it. When 100 VAC is applied across the same coil, the current drop is 0.5 A . If the frequency of the $A C$ source is 50 Hz , then inductance of solenoid is found to be $x \mathrm{mH}$, then find the value of $x$.
questions.solution:
When DC is applied across a solenoid, then resistance, i.e. $R=\frac{V}{I}R=\frac{100}{1}=100 \Omega$
When $A C$ is applied, then
$Z=\frac{100}{0.5}=200 \Omega$
Net impedance,
$\begin{aligned}
Z & =\sqrt{R^2+X_L^2} \\
200 & =\sqrt{(100)^2+X_L^2} \\
\Rightarrow (200)^2 & =(100)^2+X_L^2 \\
\Rightarrow  30000 & =X_L^2 \quad \Rightarrow X_L=173.205 \Omega
\end{aligned}$
Now, $X_L=\omega L\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow  173.205=2 \pi f L \Rightarrow \frac{173.205}{2 \pi \times f}=L \\
& \Rightarrow  \frac{173.205}{2 \times 3.14 \times 50}=L \Rightarrow 0.55 \Omega=L
\end{aligned}L=0.55 \mathrm{H}=550 \mathrm{mH}$

questions.q: In the following circuit diagram, potential difference across $4 \mu \mathrm{~F}$ capacitor is
questions.solution:
1. Parallel Combination:
The \(2 \mu F\) and \(6 \mu F\) capacitors are in parallel, so their equivalent capacitance:
\(C_{e q}=2+6=8 \mu F\)
2. Series Combination:
The \(4 \mu F^{\prime}\) capacitor is in series with the \(8 \mu F\) equivalent capacitor. The total capacitance is:
\(\frac{1}{C_{t o t a l}}=\frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{8}=\frac{3}{8} \Longrightarrow C_{t o t a l}=\frac{8}{3} \mu F\)
3. Charge Calculation:
The total charge in the circuit is:
\(Q=C_{t o t a l} \cdot V=\frac{8}{3} \cdot 12=32 \mu C\)
4. Voltage Across \(4 \mu F\) Capacitor:
Since the charge is the same in series, the voltage across the \(4 \mu F\) capacitor is:
\(V=\frac{Q}{C}=\frac{32}{4}=8 \mathrm{~V}\)
Final answer: \(\mathrm{8} \mathrm{V}\).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The stress versus strain graphs for wires of two materials $A$ and $B$ are as shown in the figure. If $Y_A$ and $Y_B$ are the Young's modulii of the materials, then
questions.solution:
We know that the slope of the line in a stress-strain curve represents the young's modulus for a wire. We also know that the slope of a line can be calculated as the tangent of the angle the line makes with the positive x -axis of the graph.
So, for wire A, the stress-strain line of the material is at an angle of \(60^{\circ}\) from the positive \(x\)-axis. So the slope of the line \(\left(m_A\right)\) will be
\(\begin{aligned}
& m_A=\tan 60^{\circ} \\
& \Rightarrow m_A=\sqrt{3}
\end{aligned}\)
Hence the young's modulus of wire A will also be \(\sqrt{3}\).
Similarly, for wire B , the stress-strain line of the material is at an angle of \(30^{\circ}\) from the positive \(x\) axis. So, the slope of the line \(\left(m_B\right)\) will be
\(\begin{aligned}
& m_B=\tan 30^{\circ} \\
& \Rightarrow m_B=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}
\end{aligned}\)
Hence the young's modulus of wire B will also be \(1 / \sqrt{3}\).
Then taking the ratio of the young's modulus for wire A and B , we get
\(\begin{aligned}
& \frac{Y_A}{Y_B}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{1 / \sqrt{3}} \\
& \therefore \frac{Y_A}{Y_B}=3
\end{aligned}\)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two pendulums of time periods 3 s and 7 s , respectively start oscillating simultaneously from two opposite extreme positions. After how much time they will be in same phase?
questions.solution:
General equation of oscillation are
$\begin{aligned}
& y_1=A \sin \left(\omega_1 t+\frac{\pi}{2}\right) \\
& y_2=A \sin \left(\omega_2 t+\frac{\pi}{2}\right)
\end{aligned}$
Now, $\omega_1 t+\frac{\pi}{2}=\omega_2 t-\frac{\pi}{2}$
or
$\begin{aligned}
t & =\frac{\pi}{\omega_2-\omega_1} \\
& =\frac{\pi}{\left(2 \pi / T_2\right)-\left(2 \pi / T_1\right)} \\
& =\frac{T_1 T_2}{2\left(T_1-T_2\right)} \\
& =\frac{3 \times 7}{2(7-3)}=\frac{21}{8} \mathrm{~s}
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: When a lens is cut into two halves along $X O X^{\prime}$, then focal length of each half lens
questions.solution:
If $R$ be the magnitude of radius of curvature of equiconvex lens, then its focal length $f$ is given by
$\begin{aligned}
\frac{1}{f} & =(\mu-1)\left(\frac{1}{R_1}-\frac{1}{R_2}\right) \\
& =(\mu-1)\left(\frac{1}{R}-\frac{1}{-R}\right)=\frac{2(\mu-1)}{R} \\
\Rightarrow \frac{1}{f} & =\frac{2(\mu-1)}{R}...(i)
\end{aligned}$
When equiconvex lens is cut into two halves along $X O X^{\prime}$, then
$R_1=R, R_2=-R\therefore$ Focal length $f^{\prime}$ is given as
$\begin{aligned}
\frac{1}{f^{\prime}} & =(\mu-1)\left(\frac{1}{R}-\frac{1}{-R}\right)=\frac{2(\mu-1)}{R}=\frac{1}{f} \quad[\text { from (i) }] \\
\Rightarrow  f^{\prime} & =f
\end{aligned}$

questions.solution:
Diode will be in forward bias when $V_i$ is greater than 10 V and it conducts till $V_i$ is 12 V .
Total circuit resistance
$=200+20=220 \Omega$
When $V_i$ is less than 10 V , the diode will not conduct due to its reverse biasing. Thus, initial current, $i_1=0$. 
When $V_i=12 \mathrm{~V}$, then diode will be in forward bias with effective voltage, $V^{\prime}=12-10=2 \mathrm{~V}\therefore$ Maximum current, $I_2=\frac{V^{\prime}}{R}=\frac{2}{220}=0.009 \mathrm{~A}=9 \mathrm{~mA}\therefore$ Change in current, $\Delta I=I_2-I_1=9 \mathrm{~mA}$

questions.q: If $E=$ energy, $G=$ gravitational constant, $I=$ impulse and $M=$ mass, then dimensions of $\frac{G I M^2}{E^2}$ are same as that of
questions.solution:
The SI unit in which $G$ is measured $=\mathrm{N}-\mathrm{m}^2 / \mathrm{kg}^2\therefore$ Its dimensions will be $\frac{\left[\mathrm{MLT}^{-2}\right]\left[\mathrm{L}^2\right]}{\left[\mathrm{M}^2\right]}=\left[\mathrm{M}^{-1} \mathrm{~L}^3 \mathrm{~T}^{-2}\right]\because$ Impulse $=$ Force \times  Time $=\left[\mathrm{MLT}^{-2}\right][\mathrm{T}]=\left[\mathrm{MLT}^{-1}\right]\because$ Dimensions for energy $=\left[\mathrm{ML}^2 \mathrm{~T}^{-2}\right]$
Now put the dimensions of $G, I, M$ and $E$ in $\frac{G I M^2}{E^2}\begin{aligned}
& =\frac{\left[\mathrm{M}^{-1} \mathrm{~L}^3 \mathrm{~T}^{-2}\right]\left[\mathrm{MLT}^{-1}\right]\left[\mathrm{M}^2\right]}{\left[\mathrm{ML}^2 \mathrm{~T}^{-2}\right]^2} \\
& =\frac{\left[\mathrm{M}^{-1} \mathrm{~L}^3 \mathrm{~T}^{-2}\right]\left[M L T^{-1}\right]\left[\mathrm{M}^2\right]}{\left[\mathrm{M}^2 \mathrm{~L}^4 \mathrm{~T}^{-4}\right]}=\frac{\left[\mathrm{M}^2 \mathrm{~L}^4 \mathrm{~T}^{-3}\right]}{\left[\mathrm{M}^2 \mathrm{~L}^4 \mathrm{~T}^{-4}\right]} \\
& =\left[\mathrm{T}^{-1}\right]=[T]
\end{aligned}$
The equation $\frac{G I M^2}{E^2}$ has dimension of time.

questions.q: Fundamental frequency of a sonometer wire is $n$, if the tension is made 3 times and length and diameter are also increased 3 times, what is the new frequency?
questions.solution:
Fundamental frequency,
$\begin{aligned}
& n=\frac{v}{2l}=\frac{\sqrt{T / \mu}}{2l}=\frac{\sqrt{T / \rho S}}{2l}=\frac{\sqrt{T / \rho \pi r^2}}{2l} \\
&\therefore n \propto \frac{\sqrt{T}}{2l}
\end{aligned}$
Given that tension, diameter and length all are made 3 times.
$\therefore n$ will become $\frac{1}{3 \sqrt{3}}$ times.
